definitions: An ethical theory developed by Immanuel Kant, stating that an action is morally right if and only if it conforms to a rule that one could rationally will to be a universal law.
A moral law that is unconditional or absolute for all rational beings and does not depend on any ulterior motive or end.
examples: Kant's philosophy is centered around the categorical imperative.
He argued that the categorical imperative demands we treat humanity as an end, never merely as a means.
